name: weekly-update-review
title: Weekly update review
description: Weekly schedule update review of a P6 project: progress, finish dates, critical path, slippage against the baseline, changes since the previous update when given, progress issues and a critical look-ahead, with fixed actions (read only). Use when the user asks for a weekly update review, a status report or how a project is progressing.

args.name: project
args.description: Project ID as shown in P6

args.name: weeks
args.description: Weeks of the critical look-ahead window from the data date

args.name: previous
args.description: Project ID of the previous update (empty: no comparison with it)

template:
Weekly update review of project {project}: progress, finish dates, critical path, slippage against the baseline, changes since the previous update when one is given, progress issues, the critical activities of the next {weeks} weeks and the actions that apply. Read only: nothing is written to the database.

This skill gives you every figure: you copy fields, you never compute them.
- reference/spec.json: the calls, the slots (each a field of one call) and the tables.
- reference/fields.md: for every slot and table column, its field, unit, format and meaning.
- reference/report.md: the report to fill.
- reference/checks.md: stop rules and checks to run before answering.
- reference/example.md: the report filled on a demo project (an example of the format, not of the figures).

Calls, in this order. Each call is one page: the report shows that page and says when there are more,
so do not read further pages.
1. sum = p6_project_summary(project="{project}"): progress, finish, baseline.
2. prog = p6_progress_check(project="{project}", sample_size=5): out of sequence, status checks.
3. cp = p6_critical_path(project="{project}", limit=15): critical activities.
4. la = p6_lookahead(project="{project}", weeks={weeks}, critical_only=true, limit=20): critical look-ahead.
5. cmp = p6_compare_projects(project="{project}", section="activities", min_variance_days=5, limit=15): slippage against the baseline. If this call returns an error, keep its message as cmp.error (its other fields are null).
6. prev = p6_compare_projects(project="{project}", other="{previous}", section="activities", min_variance_days=0, limit=15): changes since the previous update. Make this call only when <previous> is given; when it is empty, skip it (its fields are null).
Leave out an argument whose value is empty (previous).

Write the report:
1. Start from reference/report.md. Replace each slot placeholder (a slot name in curly braces) by the field
   named in spec.json slots (call and path), written in the slot's format (reference/fields.md). An argument
   written <name> in these instructions is the placeholder of that name in curly braces in report.md and
   checks.md: the value given (an empty optional argument is left out of the calls).
2. Replace each line [table: name] by that table: one row per item of its list, in the order returned, at
   most its cap, every cell in its column's format, the heads as in spec.json. A table with a totals entry
   ends with its Total row, taken from the totals of its call, never from adding the rows. Only a table
   built from the rows list of its call ends, when that call has more pages (next_offset not null), with
   the line "Showing the first <returned> of <total> <noun>." (returned and total of that call). A table
   built from another list or dict of the call (weeks, paths, roots, causes, counts...) ends with "Only the
   first <cap> <noun> are shown." when that list is longer than the cap, and never with a Showing line. An
   empty list gives the table's empty text; a call that failed or was skipped gives no table.
3. Keep the lines between [if: slot] and [end if] only when the slot is true (true, a number other than 0,
   a text or list that is not empty, an ID - name whose ID is not null), the lines between [if not: slot]
   and [end if] only when it is not; remove the markers.
4. Numbers: take the number as written in the result and round it, halves away from zero, to the decimals
   of its format (-104274.95 in n1 is -104,275.0); whole numbers and counts take a comma between thousands
   (1,227), also in the Showing lines. A null value is written as the slot's or column's none text, and so
   is an ID - name whose ID is null.
5. Never add, subtract, divide, count rows or match rows of two results: a figure that is not a slot or a
   table cell is left out. Ignore the note fields of the tools unless a slot names them.
6. Write the headings and sentences in the user's language; keep values, IDs, names and number formats
   exactly as formatted.
7. Run reference/checks.md before answering. Report a failed cross-check, never hide it; say nothing about
   the checks that pass.

For this skill:
- The actions are the fixed sentences of report.md only: add no other advice.
- previous is the Project ID of the previous update (a project or a saved baseline). Without it, call 6 is
  skipped and the report has no section Since the previous update.

files.text:
# Weekly update review of {project}

Data date {data_date}, last schedule run (F9) {last_f9}. Read only: nothing was written to the database.

[if: stale]
Warning: this project was changed after its last F9. Dates, float and critical counts are out of date until it is rescheduled in P6 (F9).
[end if]

## Progress

- Units % complete (actual / at completion units, labor and nonlabor): {units_pct}.
- Physical % complete (weighted by budget units): {physical_pct}; duration % complete: {duration_pct}; activities completed: {completed_pct}.
- Activities whose physical % and units % differ: {mismatch}.
- Baseline planned units % at the data date: {bl_planned_pct}; SPI (units, earned / baseline planned): {spi_units}.

## Finish

- Scheduled finish {scheduled_finish}, must finish by {must_finish}: {vs_must_cd} calendar days, {vs_must_wd} working days of the project calendar (positive = later).
- Baseline used: {baseline_used}. Scheduled finish against the baseline's: {vs_bl_cd} calendar days, {vs_bl_wd} working days of the project calendar (positive = later).

[if not: baseline_used]
This project has no baseline: the baseline figures are n/a.
[end if]

## Critical path

Critical: {cp_definition}. Critical open activities: {critical}; open activities with negative float: {neg_float}.

[table: critical]

## Slipped against the baseline

[if: cmp_error]
No comparison with a baseline: {cmp_error}
[end if]
[if not: cmp_error]
Matched activities finishing later: {later}; earlier: {earlier}. Cause of each finish variance, from the start variance and the duration change in working days:

[table: slip_causes]

Activities added or removed, then those whose finish moved by 5 calendar days or more, largest absolute variance in calendar days first (earlier finishes appear too; the table shows working days, so its order can differ from them). Finish variance = start variance + duration delta, in working days of each activity's calendar.

[table: slipped]
[end if]

[if: prev_dd]
## Since the previous update

Compared with {previous} (data date {prev_dd}): open activities with less total float {eroded}; open activities that became critical {became}; no longer critical {no_longer} (each project's own definition of critical). Added and removed activities first, then the largest finish changes in calendar days.

[table: prev_rows]

[end if]
## Progress issues

Out of sequence links: {oos_links}. Out of sequence option of F9: {logic_mode}.

[table: oos]

Status checks:

[table: status_checks]

## Critical look-ahead ({weeks} weeks)

Window from {la_from} to {la_to} (end excluded). Critical activities in the window: {la_critical}; of them in progress {la_in_progress}, starting {la_starting}, finishing {la_finishing}. Week 1 is the first 7 days of the window; outside = before or after it.

[table: lookahead]

## Actions

Only the actions that apply to this update:

[if: stale]
- Reschedule the project in P6 (F9) before using its dates: it was changed after its last F9.
[end if]
[if: oos_links]
- Out of sequence links: {oos_links}. Fix them before the next update.
[end if]
[if: chk_active]
- Activities in progress without an actual start: {chk_active}. Add their actual start.
[end if]
[if: chk_complete]
- Completed activities with remaining duration or no actual finish: {chk_complete}. Correct them.
[end if]
[if: chk_after_dd]
- Activities whose actual dates are after the data date: {chk_after_dd}. Correct them.
[end if]
[if: neg_float]
- Open activities with negative float: {neg_float}. Recover them: the schedule misses the must finish date or a constraint.
[end if]
[if: mismatch]
- Activities whose physical % and units % differ: {mismatch}. Check them.
[end if]
[if: la_critical]
- Critical activities in the look-ahead window: {la_critical}. Follow them up.
[end if]
[if: became]
- Activities that became critical since the previous update: {became}. Review what drives them with the planner before the next update.
[end if]
[if not: baseline_used]
- Assign a project baseline in P6 to measure slippage.
[end if]

# Checks before answering

## Stop rules (write the sentence, then stop)

- A call says the project is not found: "Project <project> was not found: check the Project ID (p6_list_projects)."
- sum.dates.data_date is null, or p6_lookahead says the project has no data date: "Project <project> has no data date: open it in P6, set the data date and run F9, then ask again."
- p6_project_summary says the project is an EPS node: repeat its message and stop.

## Warnings (kept in the report, never a stop)

- schedule_state.stale is true: the warning block of report.md and the reschedule action.
- The comparison call (cmp) returned an error, for example no project baseline: its message is written in the
  "Slipped against the baseline" section and the rest of the report is written as usual.

## Cross-checks (each group must be equal)

1. sum.schedule_state.data_date = prog.schedule_state.data_date = cp.schedule_state.data_date =
   la.schedule_state.data_date (same data date).
2. sum.schedule_state.last_schedule_date = cp.schedule_state.last_schedule_date =
   la.schedule_state.last_schedule_date (same last F9).
3. sum.critical.critical = cp.total (same critical count).
4. sum.critical.negative_float = cp.counts.negative_float.
5. sum.baseline.used = cmp.other (the comparison used the project baseline; skip when cmp failed).
6. sum.schedule_state.data_date = prev.schedule_state.data_date (only when previous is given).

If a group differs, the database changed between the calls (an F9 or an import): run the calls again
once. If it still differs, say which group differs and do not publish the figures it concerns.

## Before sending

- Every number, date and count is a slot or a table cell of reference/fields.md, copied from its field
  and written in its format. Nothing was added, subtracted, divided, counted or matched by you.
- The tables keep the rows in the order returned and stop at their cap (critical 15, slipped 15,
  since the previous update 15, look-ahead 20). A table whose call has more pages (next_offset not null) ends with its line "Showing
  the first <returned> of <total> ...", both numbers copied from that call.
- Every activity is written "Activity ID - name"; the baseline by its Project ID.
- Day columns keep their unit: (d) days of each activity's calendar, (wd) working days of each
  activity's calendar; the finish variances name calendar days and working days of the project calendar.
- The warning block is kept only when schedule_state.stale is true; an action only when its slot is true.
- The section Since the previous update is kept only when previous is given (prev ran): its counts are
  the summary fields of prev, never rows you counted.
  No other advice is added.
- Headings and sentences are in the user's language; values, IDs, names and number formats exactly as
  formatted.

# Fields of Weekly update review

Generated from reference/spec.json by the catalog build. Each slot of reference/report.md is copied from one field of one call; write it in its format, never compute it.

## Calls

1. sum = p6_project_summary(project="{project}"): progress, finish, baseline.
2. prog = p6_progress_check(project="{project}", sample_size=5): out of sequence, status checks.
3. cp = p6_critical_path(project="{project}", limit=15): critical activities.
4. la = p6_lookahead(project="{project}", weeks={weeks}, critical_only=true, limit=20): critical look-ahead.
5. cmp = p6_compare_projects(project="{project}", section="activities", min_variance_days=5, limit=15): slippage against the baseline. If this call returns an error, keep its message as cmp.error (its other fields are null).
6. prev = p6_compare_projects(project="{project}", other="{previous}", section="activities", min_variance_days=0, limit=15): changes since the previous update. Make this call only when <previous> is given; when it is empty, skip it (its fields are null).
Leave out an argument whose value is empty (previous).

## Formats

- text: the value as returned
- int: the whole number, a comma between thousands: 1,227
- date: the first 10 characters: YYYY-MM-DD
- datetime: the first 16 characters: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM
- n0: the number as written in the result rounded to a whole number, halves away from zero, a comma between thousands: 12,345
- n1: the same to 1 decimal: 12,345.6 (-104274.95 gives -104,275.0)
- n2: the same to 2 decimals: 12,345.67
- pct1: the same to 1 decimal, then %: 49.7%
- flag: yes for true, no for false
- id_name: the two fields joined: ID - Name (the ID alone when the name is null, the none text when the ID is null)
- list: the items of the list in their order, joined by a comma and a space: in_progress, finishing
- A null value is written as the slot's or column's none text (n/a unless stated).
- [if: slot] is true for true, a number other than 0, a text or list that is not empty.

## Arguments

- {project}: Project ID as shown in P6, as given
- {weeks}: Weeks of the critical look-ahead window from the data date, as given
- {previous}: Project ID of the previous update (empty: no comparison with it), as given

## Units

- wd: working days of each activity's calendar
- wd proj: working days of the project calendar
- cd: calendar days
- d: days of each activity's calendar (hours / hours per day)
- %: percent
- count: a count

## Slots

| Slot | Field (call.path) | Unit | Format | None | Meaning |
|-|-|-|-|-|-|
| data_date | sum.schedule_state.data_date |  | date | n/a | data date |
| last_f9 | sum.schedule_state.last_schedule_date |  | datetime | n/a | last F9 |
| stale | sum.schedule_state.stale |  | flag | n/a | edited after the last F9 |
| units_pct | sum.percent_complete.units | % | pct1 | n/a | units % complete |
| physical_pct | sum.percent_complete.physical | % | pct1 | n/a | physical %, budget weighted |
| duration_pct | sum.percent_complete.duration | % | pct1 | n/a | duration % |
| completed_pct | sum.percent_complete.activities_completed | % | pct1 | n/a | completed / all |
| mismatch | sum.percent_complete.units_vs_physical_mismatch |  | int | n/a | physical % and units % differ |
